readback.name: Poincare.MetricAdaptedLocalParametrix.exists_metric_adapted_local_parametrix
readback.mathematical_statement:
For every type M in universe u with a topology, a Hausdorff (T2) instance, compactness, a charted-space instance modeled on real Euclidean three-space and a smooth manifold instance for the real identity model with corners at smooth infinity (top of ENat coerced into WithTop ENat), for every supplied smooth positive-definite Riemannian metric g0 and every real alpha with 0<alpha<1, the theorem constructs an AtlasData A, scalar spatial cutoff families psi and xi indexed by Fin A.cover.chartCount, and common constants and local continuous linear maps. There are no connectedness, simple connectedness, second-countability, measurable-space, Borel, curvature, flow, Einstein-metric or sphere-recognition premises. The metric g0 remains a supplied input.
AtlasData is the actual finite extended-chart cover with anchors, open covering regions having closures inside their chart sources and compact coordinate images, and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to those regions. coordSupport A i is the image under the actual chart of the topological support of the partition function for index i. For each index, psi and xi are spatially smooth at smooth-infinity exponent, compactly supported, and everywhere valued in [0,1]. At every point of coordSupport A i, psi i equals one on a neighborhood, as stated by Filter.Eventually at nhds. xi i equals one pointwise on tsupport(psi i), without an explicit germ conclusion there. Its own topological support lies in the actual chart target, and at every point of that support the GeodesicTransport cutoff at the chart's anchor equals one on a neighborhood.
The coefficient expression is explicitly fun z => @Inv.inv (Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) real) Matrix.inv (inverseChartPullbackGramMatrixField g0 anchor z). The explicit type and instance force the nonsingular whole-matrix inverse of the actual Gram field at each spatial point. The Matrix.inv instance computes the inverse from determinant and adjugate (and zero on a singular matrix); this is not the Pi inverse which reciprocates each scalar entry. chartValue expects a coefficient function Euclidean-three-space -> Fin 3 -> Fin 3 -> real, but that function-valued expected type can no longer change this explicitly fixed inverse instance. A scoped Lean expected-type probe independently elaborated the explicit expression with Matrix.inv, while the original bare^-1 expression at the same chartValue position elaborated with two Pi.instInv instances. The earlier local-family readback's whole-matrix interpretation of that original occurrence was incorrect; its report is preserved. This correction is fully explicit in this revised literal type. On the genuine chart target the Gram field is the actual Riemannian metric in the inverse-chart tangent frame. The type exports neither an oscillation tolerance nor global off-target regularity.
There exist nonnegative Cpsi and CP and a common real tau satisfying 0<tau<=1, chosen before T. For each real T in (0,tau] there exist families P and R, which may depend on T. For each chart index, P i is a continuous real linear map from scalar Y(alpha,T) to Graph(alpha,T), and R i is a continuous real linear endomorphism of Y(alpha,T). The Y carrier represents bounded alpha Holder functions for parabolic distance norm(spatial difference)+sqrt(abs(time difference)) on [0,T] times Euclidean space, represented as zero off that cylinder. Graph stores u,ut,du,ddu in the corresponding Holder carriers, requires u(0,x)=0, ordinary spatial derivative identities up to second order on the cylinder, and HasDerivWithinAt in time within [0,T]. It does not provide ordinary time differentiability across zero or ordinary joint C3 regularity at zero.
For every chart index i, the first support property holds for all forcing f and all space-time points p: if the spatial coordinate lies outside tsupport(psi i), (P i f).u p=0. The remaining conclusions are under a separate forcing-support premise: for all p with spatial coordinate outside coordSupport A i, f p=0. Only under that premise does R i f p equal chartValue(a,P i f,p)-f p for every p, and only under that premise do both numerical estimates hold: ||R i f|| <= Cpsi*(T^((1-alpha)/2)+T^(1-alpha/2))*||f||, and ||P i f|| <= CP*||f||. chartValue is ut minus the double Fin 3 sum of the actual inverse-metric coefficients multiplied by ddu on Euclidean basis vectors. The residual sign gives operator(P f)=f+R f, not operator(P f)=f-R f. The constants are uniform over every chart and every admissible T, but these displayed residual and norm conclusions do not quantify over unsupported forcings. Continuous linearity separately implies each selected map is bounded, without asserting the displayed common norm bound on all inputs. No spatial-support property of R is explicitly exported.
This conclusion is about scalar local families. It imposes neither symmetry nor compatibility between different charts on the produced operators, and does not assert a global tensor-carrier parametrix, a right inverse or Neumann correction, nonlinear DeTurck or Ricci flow, global continuation, or a smooth limit. The Fin index may be empty; tau is still required to be strictly positive.
